Liquid cursor

Your cursor becomes liquid. Drift between floating drops, join their surfaces, and leave a little behind.

F(x,y) = Σ αrᵢ⁴ / (|p−pᵢ|² + 0.02rᵢ²)²; liquid where F ≥ 1

A FEW WAYS IN

Follow your curiosity.

Move your mouse through the artwork: the cursor itself is a liquid drop that joins the nearby surfaces. Touch and drag does the same on a phone. Click or tap to leave a new droplet. Arrow keys move the liquid cursor; Enter leaves a drop. Space scatters the drops. R or New droplets creates another arrangement. Adjust Droplets, Cohesion, Cursor size, and Drift to change the material. P freezes drift while the cursor and controls keep working. The cursor drop disappears when you leave the artwork or lift a touch. Color changes the liquid, and Save frame exports PNG. Reduced motion starts paused.

The mathematics

Each droplet contributes a smooth inverse-fourth-power scalar field. The visible liquid is the region where their sum reaches one: nearby fields make a connecting neck, while distant fields separate into drops. The cursor contributes exactly the same field as the floating drops. Cohesion scales every contribution; Cursor size sets the radius of the pointer droplet. An analytic field gradient shades a curved display surface with reflective highlights. Damped drift, short-range separation and local attraction to the cursor move the droplet centers. This is an artistic implicit-surface model, without volume conservation or a full fluid solver. Click or tap to leave another drop, up to 32; population and field evaluation are bounded for mobile devices.
